notes: One viewing, muted, from ordered frame strips of the exact preview film. Input: a tower camera's round display panning dry land. Action: smoke appears in the display, a flag box locks on it and an alert card leaves for a crew truck. Result: the alert lands on the dash phone, a clock window is marked estimated, the calendar shows no red mark, the record stays blank, a dashed line to a responder badge stops short and the plan waits on state approval. Every narrated action has a matching picture at its clause. No caption collides with a principal subject. Strips cannot show per-frame motion, so the opening pan speed is left for the timed review. story_review.one_viewing_summary: Observed in the muted phone strips. A tower camera's display pans dry land and pulls back to the tower. 16 of 56 cameras are up. Smoke appears in the display and is flagged. An alert card goes to a crew truck and lands on its dash phone. The dash clock marks an estimated window of up to ten minutes. The plume keeps burning and the cameras don't prevent fires. A dashed line from the truck stops short of a responder badge. The calendar since launch has no red mark. The response record stays blank. The plan waits on state approval.
story_review.opening_to_ending: Opens on what the camera sees and ends on the alert landed with the crew, the line to responders still open and the plan awaiting approval.
story_review.weakest_transition: s4-shot-2 to s5-shot-1: from the dash clock in the cab straight back into the lens display with no physical bridge.

subject_recognition.observed: A white camera head sits on a lattice tower top beside a large round display whose picture of red land and horizon pans as the head turns. The pull-back from 2.5 s reveals the whole tall tower with its beam over the dry plains.

contact_and_consequence.observed: The ALERT card slides out of the display's edge, shrinks onto the truck parked below and then enters the cab windshield, landing on the dash-mounted phone as a bubble that stays visible.

surface_finish.observed: The cab reads as finished with roof liner, pillars, visors, dash, wheel, a dash-mounted phone and a black dash clock with a hatched orange window. The props are flat but have edges and shading consistent with the style.

closing_payoff.observed: The top band shows the wildfire plan folder, Filed August 24th, an open State approval slot and an outlined Expected January 2027 tag. Below, the display still shows the plume, the truck carries the landed alert and the dashed line ends in a ring short of the station's badge.

dominant_action.observed: The display's own picture pans onto smoke rising from open land and the flag box closes and locks on it from 12.0 to 13.5 s, then the card performs the send from the display to the truck and onto the phone. The tags pin only after the actions.

continuity.observed: The display and head pull back to the same tower. The display that flags the smoke sends the card to the truck and that truck's cab carries the phone, clock and calendar. The display returns at 21.5 s, the tower, truck and station share the s5 wide, and the same display, truck and station return in the closing. Every frame carries the Illustration disclosure.

first_frame.observed: Frame one is the camera head and its round display already panning land, so the subject and its watching action are visible immediately.

visual_progression.observed: Display, tower, slot card, plume flagged in the display, card to the truck, cab phone, dash clock, display hold, open line, visor calendar, tailgate record, desk and composite: each shot adds a new state.

shot_variety.observed: Close display, wide tower pull-back, medium cards, cab interior medium, clock close, detail on the calendar end and empty field, and a split closing composite.

performed_turn.observed: The dashed line climbs from the truck toward the responder badge and stops with an open ring short of it, and Can share pins below. The badge sits over a tree because the station is hidden.

pace.observed: A new visible change arrives at least every 4 s and no shot runs past 5 s. The weakest interval is the 28.5 to 31.5 s visor strip, which changes little at phone size.

closing_answer.observed: The alert is landed with the crew, the line to responders stays open and the plan waits on state approval in the same frame, with no invented outcome.

finished_art.observed: The bezelled display with its compass tape and panning land, the smoke and flag box, and the cab and clock read as finished authored art. The s5 wide's occluded station is the weakest finish.

clauses.observed: The display pans the land as the head turns, then the view pulls back to the tall tower and its beam.
Lens rings light one by one to 16 installed on a card of 56.
The planned rings brighten and the 56 planned by February 2027 tag pins, with the top rows cropped.
Smoke rises from open land in the display and the flag box closes on it, with no building at its base.
The ALERT card leaves the display for the truck and lands on the cab's dash phone.
The dash clock's hatched window opens and Estimated within ten minutes pins at its end.
The plume keeps burning under the locked flag in the display and Doesn't prevent fires pins to the rim.
Wide, a dashed line from the truck's landed alert stops short of the station badge and Can share pins, the line is small.
The visor calendar runs from Launch to Now with no red mark and Per AEP's wildfire lead pins at Now.
A blank Response record slides onto the tailgate and its how much sooner field pulses and stays empty, the label is clipped.
The plan folder slides onto the desk with State approval open and Expected January 2027, then the composite holds it above the landed alert and the open line.
